study_identification_part.si_4_title: Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Centile-based normative model using GAMLSS; out-of-sample alignment with maximum-likelihood estimation of study-specific offsets for mean, variance, and skewness in an age- and sex-specific manner.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: “we used a generalized additive model for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS)”; “The out-of-sample centile method used here enabled us to calculate centiles without the need to re-train the model... using maximum likelihood to estimate the study specific offsets (random effects) for three moments of the underlying statistical distributions: mean (μ), variance (σ), and skewness (ν) in an age- and sex-specific manner.”
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: GarciaSanMartin2025.pdf.md: Centile and effect sizes estimation and analysis; GarciaSanMartin2025_sup1.docx.md: Centile-based normative model

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical gray matter regional volumes (DK atlas); 34 regional centiles averaged across hemispheres.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: “we generated centile scores for cortical gray matter (GM) phenotypes, identifying deviations in regional volumes”; “Cortical brain parcellation was performed using Desikan-Killiany (DK) atlas, and volumetric measurements were derived for each region-of-interest.”; “only 34 DK regional centiles (instead of 68) could be derived for each individual.”
nm2_2_response_variable.location: GarciaSanMartin2025.pdf.md: ARTICLE OPEN Molecular and micro-architectural mapping of gray matter alterations in psychosis; GarciaSanMartin2025.pdf.md: MRI acquisition, parcellation, and volume extraction; GarciaSanMartin2025.pdf.md: Centile and effect sizes estimation and analysis

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex terms used in centile modeling; study/site-specific offsets accounted for site effects (batch effects).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: “normalized by age-, sex- and site-effect.”; “age-normed and sexstratified measures... after adjusting for scanning site offset.”; “age- and sex-specific manner... accounting for study-specific ‘batch effects’.”
